reviews.comment: I don't think I learned anything tbh.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is quite honestly the worst professor I've had at UM. I wish I read the reviews before I signed up for his class. He stands at the board, mumbles for 70 minutes straight, and scribbles all over the board with no line of reasoning. I have not learned anything from this class. There is absolutely no structure during class. HORRIBLE.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is bad at teaching. Lecture and slides mostly useless and have to teach yourself everything. 2 midterms and a final, all take home exams so it was very doable. First midterm was each, second midterm and final was tricky. Was easy to get good grades without learning much.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Makes an intro class way more difficult than it has to be and spent 30-45 minutes each lecture just reading the textbook to us instead of teaching.

Not one to take if you value your GPA. He discouraged me from going to graduate school. His ludicrously difficult tests destroyed my confidence and constantly made me question my abilities as a math major. Overall, I studied nearly 40-50 hours a week and still could only pull of a B-. He makes this course next to impossible, please do not take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This is a core course for the stats track. If you're on this track, avoid Ille at all costs. His lectures vastly overcomplicate even the simplest concepts in stats/probability). On top of this, his accent and handwriting make following his lectures difficult. Furthermore, he's just not an engaging lecturer.
His lectures are really good for sitting and taking a few notes, but aren't mandatory by any means. You can certainly pass by learning from the textbook, doing the homework, and studing
Greatest mathematician I have ever known, the most bright man I met

This class was lacking structure. Some days Dr. Grigorescu would spend an hour deriving an equation several different ways. Other days he would apply theories and teach strategies for solving problems. Which version you get is as random as a coin flip.  First test was cake, second was significantly harder, and the final was in between.
Very confusing lectures and homework that often doesn't correlate to what was discussed in class. On tests you get to pick 5 of 6 questions to answer but still are quite difficult and specific

Im a math major focusing on prob & stat, and I struggled in this class A LOT. He has a reallllly strong accent and just lectures to the whiteboard. I couldn't hear/see anything he was doing and he never answers questions or clarifys. Exams are tough but there is a curve. Would recommend taking another prof

2 exams and one final. One homework. I love this professor but he has a decent accent. He is willing to help people. I don't why people think he is bad. The stuff that he taught is useful if you are going to get the certificate in the future. I would recommend him and take him again. I really like him. You can download the textbook online
HE KNOWS EVERYTHING AND ASSUMES YOU DO TOO. HW ARE HARD BUT THE TESTS ARE EVEN HARDER.. THE WORST CLASS I'VE TAKEN SO FAR.

rushes through important stuff, says proofs are trivial and doesn't teach how to do epsilon-delta proof. assumes class knows subject  when everybody is clearly struggling. worst professor I have had at UM
Not helpful
He's a great professor! If you like the subject you will not have any problems! Even if you struggle, his curves are extremely helpful! I reccommend him :)

He is the best calculus teacher.  His tests are not difficult and he has a generous curve.  The tests are EXACTLY like the assigned homework problems, and he is very helpful during office hours.  He also moves the test dates back if enough people ask; he's more concerned with students learning the material.  I took him for calc 1 and 2 and got A+'s
Confusing!
He is a difficult teacher. Test are moderate, got Bs. Never showed up to classes. Basically learned the material by myself, with the help of people who had other teachers. Take Agras if you can.

OK teacher. He cares more about seeing that students understand the material than making deadlines, which is good. Curves a lot. He does try, but a lot of times it's hard to understand him. The book helps a lot.

he is a nice guy but he cannot teach. our class was often found in the math lab trying to get help. really nice guy but cant get subject across. he curves really high but its to make up for his horrible teaching. stick to the book and you will be able to get through

He seems like a SUPER NICE GUY. I haven't finished his class, but he appears very willing to help you. He has alot of the characteristics that make a great teacher. But I can see calcII requires interest from the student more than anything else.
hes really easy on curving
This professor was very clear in his approach to calc 2.  His curves are ridiculus and it is very easy to get a good grade
ok
No Comments

I was really nervous about taking BSL 212 but he made it easy to understand. He isn't a tough grader at all. There were times I completely chose the wrong party to win and somehow got a decent grade. I took his class online over the summer so if you were wondering, he requires that you have your camera on. Overall, really chill and a great teacher!

This is the third class I've had with Professor Karamoko and he's truly the best professor at UMiami. He's incredibly knowledgable about the law and he makes lectures so interesting. Exams aren't the easiest but he's clear on what you need to study and gives a practice exam. He makes an effort to get to know you and really cares about his students.

Jelani is a straightforward and engaging professor. He does not allow computers in class. He gives all the info you need during the lecure, he grades fairly, and you must brief one case during class for participation. His lectures are interesting and often funny, and he explains the material clearly. I would take him again!

How to Succeed in class Part 2:
1.) Participate in one discussion (throughout the semester he has case studies - you read a case from the chapter and he asks you questions about it - in order to get credit you only need to do this once in the whole semester)

He is a very easy grader. Even if you get a question wrong he gives you partial credit.

How to succeed (part 1):
1.) He takes attendance every day (it counts towards grade)

2.) Take notes in class, you don't actually have to read textbook - everything on the quizzes comes from his lectures
       - Beginning of class he writes down notes on board and goes through it (he explains it very simply and is always open to questions)

Genuinely one of the best prof. Lectures are organized for note taking and you can tell he puts effort into them. Even if you are not getting all the answers right (or any) on quizzes, as long as you participate in class, do the homework, and show that you studied the topics you will still get a good grade. Literally took an 8am to have him again.

I took his class for business law and BUS300 and absolutely loved him in both. You have to show up to class and participate, but he makes his classes as enjoyable as possible and you actually look forward to going. His grading is very fair - although sometimes he takes a while to get the grades back to you. I would take him for any business class!

Karamoko is a very enthusiastic and fair professor, and I enjoyed taking him for BSL333. While he does have an irregular attendance and participation scheme, where he awards "gold stars" and tracks attendance on flash cards, he is solid. This course is best taken as a longer block, not a 3x a week course.

Professor K is the best professor at UM! He makes me almost excited to wake up for his 8am lectures. Business Law is one of the hardest core classes for the Business School but he grades very fairly and offers a lot of help inside and outside of class. Looking forward to his BSL 333 Class! Highly Recommend!

Overall a good professor. No surprise that business law has a lot of content to go through, just wished he had moved a little faster so that we wouldn't have to do quizzes right up until the final. A lot of memorization for this class, but the professor is funny and is great at using easy examples to help explain concepts. Quiz almost every week.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Karamoko was great at explaining the law during his class. He went at a pace that everyone could understand.  He moved almost too slowly at first to where we had our last quiz during the last class only a few days before the final.  The final for this class is a group one and difficult but he is a very fair grader and I recommend taking him.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He gave us an exam the day after halloween than proceeded to not show up for the exam. Other than that, I loved this class and learned a lot.

One of the best professors I've ever had. If you can take him! There's quizzes which is the majority of your grade, but he doesn't grade harshly and if you attend class you will understand everything.

He grades based on 3 exams and if you like your grade, you drop the final. We took the exam on Friday and he said that we will get our exams back on Monday since the final was on Wednesday and we had to let him know by end of day Monday if we were taking the exam. Its Monday at 9pm and we don't have our grades and he hasn't answered any emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love professor Karamoko. He is seriously so intelligent and makes learning the law so much easier than it is. We have 5 quizzes, a writing assignment (in class, only two paragraphs), and a final. He isn't a tough grader compared to other Business Law professor's. Study hard for each exam and you will be sure to get an A! Love him so much. GOAT

Great professor all in all, great lectures and time really flies by. Quizzes seem easier than they really are - lots of trick questions. Little hard to reach him out of class, but good class and prof. overall

He cares about his students and is overall a chill guy. Very personable and understanding, W professor.
(also, the class playlist of recommended music before we dive into the material is 10/10 great, I never had a professor do that, but they should start)

Graded off just 5 quizzes, 1 paper, and 1 final. Such a relaxed and professional professor and emphasizes how to simplify and talk about the lessons clearly so everyone understands. Last couple of quizzes were rushed at the end of semester, but is just a goat in teaching. Study the rules of law and case studies and you will ace every quiz.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was definitely one of the harder classes of the semester. I am not a business/law student, so others might think it was easier. The only grade was 3 quizzes, so if you do badly on the quizzes you're screwed. His class is a lot of teaching yourself out of the classroom prior to the quizzes. Overall, he's great but I wouldn't take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor and one of the nicest I have ever had. Extremely accommodating to all of the students' desires. Quizzes are very fair and class is a very chill environment with him. I can't stress enough to take him as a professor.

As someone who's 212 professor rushed through content, I was nervous for this class. However, Karamoko is great. He explains each concept in detail and doesn't rush so the class understands each concept clearly. The class is not hard if you attend class, otherwise, you'll have a hard time. Super nice & professional guy too, def get to know him too.
Great professor he wants the class to learn. Just very quiz/test heavy. Be ready to buy the textbook and essentially teach yourself.

Prof Karamoko is a great teacher! He is very relaxed with his teaching style and explains complex topics in ways that are easy to understand. I feel prepared for every assessment and enjoy the material in the class because he engages everyone and helps us thoroughly understand the topics in BSL 212.

Professor Karamoko engages in his lectures and really makes you understand the material. I loved him. You have one big paper on a movie and a few tests. The tests are written response and only two questions (multiple parts), but he gives you as many points as possible. The final exam is very stressful, just take the time to study and MEMORIZE.

Was an amazing professor, very down to earth and wants students to succeed. Made all of the concepts easy to understand and did everything he could to help students who were struggling. Would totally take him again.

He explains each concept with examples, just go to class and skim over the chapters outside of class and you'll be fine. Grade is based off of 5 quizzes, a paper, and a final. The quizzes are tough sometimes but he is an is an insanely understanding grader.
W Teacher
Chill prof. lectures were pretty boring but the tests were decently easy especially with the cheat sheet allowed.

The most boring lecturer I have ever had. Impossible to listen because he just reads from the textbook. The exams are alright if you do homework. Also includes several group projects on R that he does not talk much about

Jason Grant is easygoing, but his lectures are not helpful; he is quite literally an human audio book. He rereads the textbook without adding explanation or insight. Questions are answered by repeating the book. No practice exams or review materials are given, aside from extremely lengthy homework (ungraded btw). 90%  of students stopped attending.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Easygoing personality, but not a strong lecturer. Classes consist of reading directly from the textbook and rewriting it on the board, with little added explanation or engagement. Questions often aren't addressed in a helpful way. No practice exams are provided, which makes preparing for tests more difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Reads the textbook verbatim. Extra credit on a random class where a few people attend, worth 5 points. Class is boring and I learned everything myself. Exams are pretty easy if you exhaust questions from the homework.
Cool guy but lectures are awful. Better off learning it by yourself. Not the person you want to be with if you actually want to learn statistics.

Doesn't give any partial credit on his tough exams. Lectures are him reading from his physical textbook. If you want to keep up with the material, you need to have the textbook up and keep up. Very boring. Also, he uses the same tests for both sections, so one section has to study for exams and the other has a cheat sheet with the exam on it.

If you want an easy A, id take him. He lets you bring in a whole page cheat sheet so you can just cram for the 2 tests with that and he's an awesome guy. If you wanna actually learn stats, I would look elsewhere. No-one listens (or even attends) lectures as he just reads straight from text.

Very unstructured. Lectures are literally just reading the book. You get to use a cheat sheet on all the tests. All assignments were pretty easy and straight forward. You're best bet if you have to take him is to just read the book and do the practice problems during lecture and only use him to ask questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He just stood up in front of the class and read the textbook. Seemed like he had never taught this class before. Really nice guy but seemed like he had no interest in what he was "teaching". I could have never went to class and probably gotten the same grade. Test problems are right from the textbook.

This class is so easy as he explains from day 1 it's an "introductory class" and he treats it that way. He will always help with any question/lab and makes sure everyone is on the same page. Definitely take this class, he is super nice and laid back.

Lots of unnecessary hate by those unwilling to listen to his advice on how to handle the class. Content is tough,but he simplifies hard concepts well. His lectures are conversational,he's always open to questions,and gives great study advice in office hrs.He did everything he could to help me pass considering my difficulty w the online exam format.

Prof Wilson is a really nice and funny guy, but hes pretty unorganized and lectures aren't helpful. i learned everything from the textbook, and if you attend lectures read the content before and you might learn something in class. orgo 2 is challenging and i dont think any of the profs are super helpful, book + practice are probably your best bet.

Professor James is really good at what he does. His lectures are very straightforward, it's hard sometimes because it's so much material. Orgo2 is the kind of class where if you did bad you were going to do bad anyways. Don't blame the professor because the subject is hard.

Do NOT take him. He guaranteed me a passing grade, knowing my situation as a pre-med student, but bailed last second and gave an unexpected grade. Despite attending every workshop and office hour, I got just 1% extra credit. His teaching is terrible—lectures rely on confusing packets, and I learned nothing beyond the textbook. U teach urself
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Wilson is GREAT for HHMI. He is funny, all over the place, and just made lab fun to go to. I will miss having him as my instructor!

Dr. Willson is great for HHMI. He is easy to understand and makes the process stress-free. You will learn to love how he runs the lab, and it will become something you look forward to weekly. There are no quizzes, and he gives you great feedback on what you are doing wrong about your experiment and ways to improve it! Take him for HHMI!

I taught myself this entire course. Once I realized that the lectures were no help at all, I skipped every class and read the textbook instead. Unlike with orgo I, everyone in is highly motivated and extremely smart, so simply understanding the content is not enough. Doing well in this class is dependent on who has put in the most time and effort.

Half of the time you fear he blew up his lab, other half he hand-waved another exam question out of thin air.
Man goes on tangents and exhibits these quirks when he loses  his train of thoughts (laughing and hand waving).

Wilson is the GOAT. Class is tough, but makes you aware of what you gotta do to succeed. Best strategy is to read and take notes before lecture; he provides a schedule of what's taught everyday and the recommended reading. He gives some chances to boost your grade too. JW cares about his students and does what he can to help you out. He's a beast!

Literally didn't cover half of the content that would be on exams. He's a nice guy who's willing to help you, but TOLD US in class that hes not good at teaching and its true. Our class average was lower than the other professors on the same exam. If i could go back I'd do anything to not take him again.

Dr. Wilson is a nice guy but his lectures are no help. He spends his time in class speeding through the material, assuming we already understand the topics. He gives very unclear answers to questions and ignores negative feedback because the class is a weed out. He makes an already hard class much worse. I honestly taught myself the course.
Doesnt have a teaching degree and blames that on the grades he gives people

Professor Wilson is a nice person, but this man cannot teach organic chemistry. He goes over naming the molecules for the whole class and useless info instead of information that is practical on the test. The test questions are very difficult and reflect barely anything learned in class and are made to confuse the student. This class sucks.

His tests are hard, but he is always available to help. The lectures get very boring, but I'm sure that's for all Orgo classes because the material is just dense. He curves at the end so as long as you're doing better than the other students, your raw score doesn't really matter. He doesn't give practice tests/study guides so you have to wing it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Wilson is my favorite professor & I'm sad that I can't take him next semester due to schedule reasons. I was initially very scared of ochem as it's considered a "weed out", but Dr. Wilson is nothing of that sort & makes ochem very enjoyable. I can't emphasize enough to read the textbook,practice problems, flashcards, he will not spoon feed you.

I hate Wilson. He uses his "nice guy" attitude to hide the fact that he shows literally no empathy towards his students. I am a good student, I got all A+'s in my other classes and I have to retake CHM222. He refuses to curve the grades even though the exam average at the end was a 62%. He's also very forgetful and doesn't answer any emails.

Absolutely horrible! Do not take this class if you want to best learn orgo. His lectures barely even reflect what was on the exams. Also, he doesn't even get to see the exams before they are given, so he doesn't even know what is on the tests until he grades them. Just horrible, avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Do not take Dr. Wilson. He canceled class for iffy-at-best reasons, and when we did have class his notes came from textbook examples. He is also EXTREMELY hard to reach, and will not respond to your emails unless you repeatedly attempt to get in contact. You're better off learning from the textbook and only going to class to supplement the reading.

Dr. Wilson is a nice guy but DO NOT TAKE for orgo 2. Class is hard yes but he is unaccessible (literally ignored my emails for days) and would randomly cancel class because of "wifi issues" and other reasons. Class averages were never above a D on exams and he did nothing to help grades. Lectures were so unclear and he went so fast no one learned.
Wilson is a very good professor and he cares about his students. The class is hard but thats with every and any professor. Just put in the work and you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This man is so frustrating. Orgo 2 is hard enough and he does not teach it well. He goes through notes so fast and would switch slides before you can finish writing. He pretty much copy and pastes notes from the book. what would be more helpful is if he did hypothetical test or hw questions in class. hw & discussion don't prepare you for the exam.

Worst thing to happen was for this class to be online. SO FAR no partial credit on exams, either u got the points or didn't, which is not fair. Never responds to emails, on the rare occasion u meet, he ends it after 1 min. Doesn't seem to really care about his class or students. Was actually trying so hard to participate but didn't even matter.

He cancels class constantly for the most ridiculous reasons and he never answers emails. Never. If you have a pressing issue, good luck, because he isnt there to help you ever. He is honestly awful. He rarely does office hours as well. I wouldve rather taken anyone else, even Colonna.

I worked extremely hard, 90+ hours for each test (studied 2 weeks before each), knew the material as if I memorized the textbook & still think this class was extremely unfair in the test material. 1st test had questions that were so irrelevant to the chapters & the lectures don't help at all so I stopped going. just read the textbook learn yourself

Class is not clear. Everyone is confused and yes, organic chemistry 2 is very difficult in itself however, with no clear instruction we all feel as if we won't pass the class. Exams should be open book. It is already an expensive class, if we only we actually learned.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: JW is da man! He's very approachable and his lectures are engaging. He works out problems step-by-step on the board, which helped me learn better. The best way to study is to work out ALL or MOST of the problems in the back of the textbook before each test and to go to his office if you need anything clarified.
Class is confusing, you're better off teaching yourself. Exams are ridiculous, most of the class doesn't do well. Go with another teacher, don't risk your GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Wilson is the man. He wants you to succeed. The curve for Fall 2018 was really big, so like 86+ was an A. The class really depends on whether or not you understand organic chemistry though. If you don't, you're screwed. He'll help you, but it's up to you to learn it yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: i like him he is interesting

I never went to class that much but Dr. Wilson provides you will all the tools to succeed in his class. Honestly, I learned a lot from reading the textbook, but his notes are great and he truly is the best Organic Chemistry professor at UM. After suffering through Murthy for a whole semester, my friends and I agree we learned much more with Wilson.

What the syllabus doesn't tell you and what dr. Wilson doesn't tell you unless you ask is that only a certain % (about 20%) of people can get A's lmao so now that you know that... your classmates are your competition hahaha

Orgo 2 is absolutely a difficult class and only something like the top 20% can get A's so... that can be good news depending on how you look at it lol. Dr. Wilson is hands down the best professor I've had at UM though, good enough to make Orgo 2 my favorite class! Definitely take him if you can, I mean I got an A+ so its not THAT bad lol
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Wilson for HHMI, and it was a great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: He does a partially flipped class, so he expects you to read and know material before class. He's a nice guy that answers questions well, although he goes a little fast through the material. He is a solid choice, although you will have to do a lot of reading in the book to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: As a person, Wilson is great. He's funny & quirky, which makes lectures interesting. It's a flipped classroom, so he expects you to read before class & gives tophat quizzes every class, but you can talk during quizzes. He lectures really quickly so you'll have to rely on the book for mechanisms. Tests are okay if you study a lot before, he curves.

Dr. Wilson is funny and caring however he is very confusing. He is extremely intelligent however he is not a good lecturer, is often unclear with assignments, and is unsure when answering questions. However if you work with him he will work with you and he wants everyone to do well.

He doesn't successfully break down/explain the material in a way for students to understand. Most of the time you're teaching  yourself. Read book before lecture for the  in class quiz questions. Don't expect a big curve at the end - only top % of class will get a good grade. The exams are application based/hard. Take another professor if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very intelligent man who has a very difficult time presenting material. Does a lot of "hand waving" when he doesn't know the answer and directs you to the book by saying "blah blah" in his notes. NECESSARY to read the book. Have to go to class because quizzes everyday.

Look, orgo is hard no matter who you take. You basically have to dedicate your entire life to this class. Wilson is definitely the *better* orgo professor out there, so I would recommend him. You have to read the book, which actually helps, since his lectures can be all over the place.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Wilson is so amazing! Yes, orgo is difficult but if you go to his office hours and ask for help, he will definitely help with anything you need.  Great person overall!

The tests are hard, but they are the same no matter which professor you take so you might as well take the better one. If you're stuck between him and Knecht or Colonna, go with Wilson. He makes the class as fun as he can and he's a great guy who cares about his students. You must read the textbook AND go to classl! I cannot stress that enough.

Organic Chemistry is a beast. This section was jointly taught by Wilson/Colonna this semester, and anyone at Miami knows her reputation. The tests were extremely difficult, but not impossible. Wilson honestly made me appreciate orgo, and I have a solid grasp of the material. Still highly recommend the sequence, orgo will be hard no matter what.

I fell in love with Dr. Wilson this semester.  He is an amazing professor that doesn't just care about his students, but puts them even before himself.  The class is tough (expected), but not impossible, and if you put in the effort and visit Dr. Wilson in office hours, you will undoubtedly feel secure that you can conquer organic chemistry.

Amazing person outside of class, but i recommend you bring some kind of chemistry translator because he makes things unnecessarily confusing and hard. Your better off reading the book then going to class

I LOVE Wilson. Best professor I've ever had & he genuinely cares about your success. If you go to his office & show him you're actually trying, he'll help you with anything. Super nice guy; definitely has ADD & very hyper but he's a funny guy overall. Loved him & his class & I can't wait to take him again next semester. He made me love orgo so much

Dr. Wilson is a really great guy but his lectures can be a little all over the place and hard to follow. Going to class is essential to get a good grade, but it takes more than that. You will probably need to go to office hours for clarification and extra help. The class is hard by nature, no matter who you take. I would recommend Dr. Wilson.

Class is tough, but it is orgo. He really wants students to do well and is not one of those orgo professors that wants all their students to fail. Make sure to go to class, though he can sometimes be all over the place, it helps. And textbook reading is essential.

He is very unorganized all the time, as if he doesn't know what he is supposed to be lecturing. Often he makes mistakes, then tells the students to figure out what he did wrong as a homework assignment because he can't even figure it out. The textbook is super helpful because he is not. He has print out notes, but doesn't follow them closely.

He is a good teacher, but he moves around a lot and switches from topic to topic. Show up to class, take notes, PRACTICE PRACTICE PRACTICE, and ask questions. Also, get a molecular model kit because it will definitely help. He's a really nice guy with great TAs.
Great

What to say about Wilson... I mean, he is such a nice guy, but his lectures are lacking. Maybe because it's the accelerated 3 semester chem track, but he speeds through the info in class, and I had to teach myself.  The textbook will become your BFF. Some exam Qs are ridiculous, others are doable. He helps in office hours.  He's still a great guy.
Awesome guy. I graduated in 2012, one of my favorite professors.

The best organic chemistry professor at UM.  His lectures are clear and his tests are reasonable, unlike every other orgo professor at this school except Dr. Harris.  He actually cares about your grades.  I HIGHLY recommend him.
Dr. Wilson was an awesome chemistry teacher.  Funny guy, made orgo interesting.  Very easy especially compared to other orgo professors.
not good

Really good orgo professor. The structure of the PRISM class is much easier than regular orgo. Easy quizzes and homework that the TA's do for you, but the final exam was hard, not gonna lie. IF you can go into the final with a very high average you'll be fine to get an A or A-.
Great class! Got an A and didn't have to study as hard as I thought. Tests aren't bad at all. Definitely easier than the other ochem teachers.
Easiest Orgo teacher at UM. Definitely recommend him!

Great class! Sometimes a little hard to follow (partly because the subject is difficult) but if you read the book you shouldn't have trouble doing well and understanding the material. Ask questions in class and go in and talk with him because he really knows the subject and explains things well when he knows his students don't understand.
This professor is phenomenal. He makes class so much fun and you won't want to miss it...it will make you want to be a chem major! And we are all in love with him. Simple as that.

He was very hard to understand in lectures. I took AP Calculus AB in high school and still struggled in his class. VERY homework-heavy to the point where I felt I was just trying to finish the homework and not genuinely learning the material. The tests were also very hard.
He is not the best at the teaching, but he is such a nice grader and is understanding.

He's a nice guy, but not a great professor. His lectures are hard to follow. I did well in a high level calc course in high school, and I still struggled in this class. He grades super hard, and there are no reviews for the class so, it is difficult to study. If you do have him use the textbook and pray.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: this guy is the number 1 professor to AVOID in the math department. impossible to understand. makes things as easy as limits impossible to understand. I swear to you...do NOT take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't really understand the bad reviews, though he can be a bit difficult to understand. However, he is the nicest guy and is always willing to help you if you do not understand something. Calc II is just a hard course in general, its not his fault. Gives extra credit questions on exams which is clutch.
Kaiqi is one of a kind. Actually one of the hardest classes I've taken in my life, not just at UM. Will not give any points on re-grades. Avoid.

He is genuinely the worse professor I have ever had. Everything he explains only makes sense to him. I cant understand anything he is trying to say and it could be the easiest problem and he overcomplicates it. DO NOT TAKE HIM.

Dr. Yang is a very kind and caring professor. He is highly approachable outside of class and goes out of his way to help his students. While Dr. Yang's teaching style may not suit everyone, he is always willing to provide extra help when needed. As the course is challenging, Dr. Yang grades generously and is understanding of his students needs.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Grades too easy on the exams that his students average at least 5% lower on the final. hard to understand, but overall a nice guy. just a hard class with not the best fit for a professor.
Legit doesn't know what he's talking about
awful worse professor ever

I do want to say I have never taken a calc class before so tbf keep that in mind. However, his teaching style is something that makes sense in his head and his head only. He is kind, as people have mentioned, but his teaching style is too whack to make up for it. If math is not ur strong suit, he doesn't make concepts understandable :/.

He is so nice, but genuinely explains topics in such a difficult manner. He confuses everyone. It will be the simplest thing and he overcomplicates it. Unless you have taken some type of calculus before this class is very difficult. Be prepared to teach yourself.

Professor Yang can be hard to follow sometimes. However, he is very kind and is always willing to help. Calc 2 is just a hard-ish class no matter who you take, so be prepared to study a lot, especially for the cumulative final.

Most wholesome teacher you will ever have. Goes above and beyond to help his students. The math department is NOT GOOD here so he's a diamond in the rough. He tries to be as clear and easy as possible for every and is just an all around goat.
This professor explains the coursework in such a chaotic, long and unecessary way. hard to understand and follow what he is teaching. would not reccomend taking any of his courses.

Prof Yang is a very nice guy, but the way he thinks is too advanced for a beginner-level calculus class. I was really struggling to understand his lectures but was able to squeeze out an A with help from the TA and lots of tutoring. He ended up curving final grades. Overall an okay class, but you have to be ready to put in the extra time.

He's too young to be teaching a calculus class. I blame the math department of UM for getting such an inexperienced teacher to lead such an integral class. As for the professor himself, he teaches from the PowerPoints and doesn't teach problems in class. When he teaches, it feels like he expects us to already know how the math works.

Useless. As a STEM major, difficult classes are expected, but not for them to be self-taught. Lecture consists of powerpoints explaining theorems, but not how to actually solve problems. Going to class only made the material more confusing.

He knows his content, but his teaching is very poor and often confusing. If you study outside of class and do the test reviews, you will be ok The class is very quiz-heavy, almost every week. The TA was terrible for our class, and she taught the discussions. Don't be lazy, and you will be ok

Very nice guy that tries his best. The horrible ratings come from people who didn't put in enough effort to study and pass. You will have to learn by yourself, but with the right resources and enough practice you will pass. The study guides he posts for the exams are the key to success. Would take again.

He is an awful teacher, I learned nothing in this class. I am struggling so much, the TA is the only reason I am even still surviving. If Jon is the TA again, go to discussion and not lecture, because Dr. Yang is too confusing and Jon explains it 10x better. Do not take Dr.Yang if you can. He is a really nice guy though, just a terrible professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mentally he is very complex but physically very simple.

Very nice guy and I'm sure he tries his best to convey the subjects in which he feels comfortable. However, his teaching style relies heavily on prior knowledge and so called "easy steps". Doesn't show work on problems and basically relied on organic chemistry tutor and khan academy to barely sneak by.

You're better off not going to class. He cannot explain concepts to save his life and tests are not based off of the review material. Comeplty out of touch and relies on the TA to teach the topic. The worst class I have taken at UM and it pains me because he's a nice guy just should not be teaching.
If you didn't take calc in high school you won't learn it here either. Had to teach myself everything, really nice guy but wow
If my options of professors to take calc 2 with again were a horse and Kaiqi Yang I'd be out buying carrots
Genuinely a sweet heart, but really should not be a math teacher. I have had to teach myself everything this semester. I'm not even sure he understands calculus (or english).

Horrible math teacher. His lectures are only confusing textbook slideshows. Skips steps when performing examples. He simply doesn't explain concepts well and he forced me to try and learn the material outside of class all semester. Tests are extremely hard!! DON'T TAKE HIM unless you have taken Calc 2 in the past or you will struggle.

Terrible teaching, doesn't even understand calculus, unless you are a math wiz you are certain to struggle with him, avoid at all costs please or just take Calc II over the summer at your community college. Calc II is a very hard subject and this teacher makes it 10 times worse

Was his first time teaching and it did not go well. Very nice man but we relied on our discussion teacher to learn anything. Only reads off of ppt textbook definitions or proofs. I have taken calc before and his teaching style honestly made me more confused. He is truly trying his best but needs to change a lot about his teaching style.

I really enjoyed the summer course. She was really nice and I didnt think it was too hard however I think if it was not online in the summer it would have been a lotttt harder. The summer course made assignment turn around very quick but she grades fast. I enjoyed the class but AP Style quizzes were hard and shes a tough grader. Super sweet prof

This was one of my harder classes but I do think that Tiffani is a good professor. There were a total of 5 punctuation quizzes but if you genuinely study you will do fine, I didn't get less than a 85%. There's a lot of extra credit opportunities aswell. You need to keep up on your own, she doesn't always announce homework. But overall positive.

were made overly complicated, attendance was harshly enforced (3 absences meant failure, even excused), yet the professor sometimes missed class without notice. Weekly punctuation quizzes felt pointless and overly tricky, and no slides were posted to Canvas, making the course poorly organized.

This is for STC 346. gives a lot of extra credit if your grade is bad. There's a lot of group work, but you get to pick your partner. Lots of assignments, so you need to stay on top of that. I've taken her 3 times, so I recommend her. The only bad thing I would say is that her directions are really confusing and all over the place sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This professor consistently made the class harder than it needed to be. Her directions were often poorly written and very difficult to understand which caused a lot of confusion for simple assignments. Communication was unclear and many students ended up having to ask for clarification on things that should have been straightforward.
Really nice professor, class is pretty interesting. Lots of extra credit opportunities, highly recommend!

I enjoyed being in Dr. Snowden's class. She made the subject interesting and shared real life experiences. I also had the opportunity to travel with her to a mission trip in Haiti in 2018, in which I had the privilege to work alongside her and learn from her. I am fortunate to have met Dr. Snowden. She made a significant impact on my nursing career
Be prepared for lots of "um's" in lecture. She's nice and will hear you out. Her exams are easy-for example, for a "select all" question, she'll say "choose 3", which is very appreciated.

Dr. Snowden is super sweet. No one ever paid attention in her class bc it was literally only an hour long. Attendance was for a grade and we had in class assignments that you needed to be in class for. Exams were easy (got As just by reading the ppts) but some ppl said they were hard lol. Would take her again
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Twichell is the man! He is super passionate about what he teaches, and cares about all of his students. He is a super engaging lecturer, and requires participation and being active in class. Make sure to pay attention to his reviews before every exam, as they help quite a bit. Can't wait to take more classes with him!

Professor prioritizes attendance and participation over actual academic performance. I maintained an A/high-A average on academically graded work and still lost my A because of participation and attendance. The class felt more focused on busy work and compliance than actual learning. Also came across as very condescending toward students.

He's such a passionate teacher and cares deeply about his students and what hes teaching them. Exams were tough but good once you studied. Final essay great way to boost your grade as long as you're careful. Homework wasn't checked, but do it for your own benefit. I really liked him overall even if lectures were boring at times.

One of the best teachers I've ever had, he is extremely knowledgeable and truly cares a lot about what he does, and that reflects extremely well in his lectures which are engaging and are great to listen to. On top of all of that, he is very reasonable, understanding better than 99% of professors that sometimes things go wrong. 10/10, taking again.

I have taken several courses with Dr. Twichell, and I can say he's one of the best. He really cares about what he is teaching and keeps up with you as the semester progresses, making sure you understand the information. He cares about his students and their interests, making sure to always encourage them or help them academically.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Honestly, one of my most interesting classes. He is very lecture heavy and does want you to participate, but I learned so much that I would for sure take him again. My class was graded on 3 exams, class participation and a final paper, but he goes over the each exams reviews a while in advance and makes sure youre prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class is not difficult if you actually show up, most annoying part was the attendance grade. Other than that you have to make a blog which is super easy, and then the 2 exams. You do have to read the material for the exams but if you can yap they are also fairly easy. Be prepared to not miss class bc ur grade will suffer.

Great teacher! Genuinely cares about each and every one of his students and you aren't just a number. He might call on you sometimes but make sure you just do the readings. His lectures are actually interesting. Grade is based on essay exams mostly and your wordpress project which is pretty simple if you genuinely care about it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Twichell is the most passionate teacher I've had, and his approach ensures real engagement by making us lead discussions rather than just posting readings like others professors. The inclass essays are hard (I had an 80 percent average). 585 is not an easy A but if you prepare (essays are on lockdown browser), you'll be rewarded.
Great young man, knows his stuff

John Twichell was a great professor! He is extremely passionate about Latin American Studies and loves all his students. You have readings for every class but I got by only reading a summary of each. The blog post assignments are easy as long as you plan them out. He posts all the exam questions before the exams so you can prepare.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The best...he cares so much about his students and wants them to succeed. He's also super accessible through his office hours and makes every class meaningful. You have to put the work in, but you learn so much that it's totally worth it. I have taken several of his classes and have only ever had a positive experience!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Talk in class for homework days (pretty easy hw), and you'll do great. He goes over test questions in class, and all of the material is on his powerpoints. While attendance and participation do matter, honestly he's a great guy and professor. Only downside is if your class is online, you have to have your camera on. Recommend!!

If you don't like to participate, give 10-minute speeches, and get cold-called, then don't take his classes. He is extremely knowledgeable, but he expects too much from his students. I didn't have to study much for his class because most of the work was done in the class. Even though it wasn't the hardest, it was the class I least looked forward to

To pass the class you just have to complete the assignments to his liking. he is accessible outside of class which is helpful, however class time was very ineffective and repetitive, and we did not really learn anything the entire semester.

HW everyweek, but if you do it and answer questions it REALLY helps you. Talk in his class and you will get a good grade, be prepared for the first test and know how to study for it. He can kind of be scary  but he he just expects that people talk in the class.

I have learned SO much in this class. I feel so much more knowledgeable about the subject thanks to him. There is a LOT of work in the class, specifically reading and writing, but as long as you do it, you will get the grade you want. He is very understanding, and cares a lot about the subject and his students.

Dr. Twichell is a very knowledgeable person, but requires participation in a class that is extremely extremely boring. A lot of the class is him lecturing with no background media (powerpoint etc) and randomly calling on students. He also tends to call on the same student for an entire class. Class is mandatory for INS major, so just brace yourself

WOW! One of the most miserable people I have ever met. A lot of your grade is based on participation and he has had a rude remark every time I participated. He clearly has this weird anger inside about "our generation" because he goes on rants every class about how lazy we are. he simpilly CANNOT speak w/o a disgustung tude.

His class is definitely not the easiest but this is a class I can honestly say I learned a lot. He's INCREDIBLY knowledgable and accommodating and often gives some answers to test questions in class. His powerpoints are long but super helpful and he highlights the most important points. Take him!!!

As an INS major, I've taken four classes with him. He can be very condescending and rude at times, but no one can tell me that man isn't extremely knowledgable and passionate about what he teaches. Not my fav professor, but have definitely learned A LOT from him. INS 201 was the only class I don't recommend taking w him (scroll down). Overall good

Alright, not sure why this professor has so many bad ratings. This class was very straightforward, no homework, tests are not hard at all, and he is super chill. Like I don't know why people hate on him. This was easily my favorite class of the semester because of the content and teacher. if you want a easy and straightforward class, take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: What I liked about his class was he was very straightforward about grading and was clear about the material that was on the midterms and final. There are no surprises and his expectations are very clear. He is funny and very engaging in class. Before taking him, I only heard bad things but he was my favorite professor this semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He has improved since the beginning of the semester but he is still hard to tolerate. The first half of the course is very lecture heavy, and then the entire second part of the semester is a large group project. You probably have to take this course, so my advice is to study his slides before an exam, do well on the projects, and you will be fine.

Honestly, I don't know what a lot of other people went through during this class but it was honestly fine. He seemed to have improved a lot. Everything is pretty straight forward and easy to follow. Put in the work and be direct with questions and things will be fine. While he may not be super friendly, he will help you.

Really not a difficult class, but he is a harsh grader if you aren't on his good side and he sometimes comes around as arrogant. However, I did appreciate him as being a strict grader since he tries to get the most out of his students and it showed in presentations and cases. Tests aren't bad.

Professor Korogodsky is a good professor, and underrated. If you can understand his sense of humor you will like this class. If you put the time and effort into the three group projects you will get a good grade. He prepares you to become a better public speaker. If you pay attention during the lectures you will do well on the exams.

Korogodsky does not care if you succeed in the slightest. The team cases don't have to do with the course material, are graded harshly and he jumps in out of nowhere to interrupt. He clearly knows his technology because he catches students sharing attendance codes and I have seen many bad reviews disappear from this website... avoid if possible.

prof is really interested in the material. He is just very strict and has very specific rules that if you don't follow he makes a fool out of you. His class is definitely the hardest BTE210 class compared to the other classes. We had to do case studies (3+ hours a day) when other classes just had to present simple power points like "what is apple."

Honestly, all the reviews on here are a bit of an exaggeration. For the team projects and presentations: as long as you know what you're presenting and you're not reading off of the slide, he won't criticize you. I wont lie, though, this class was hard and time consuming, but not the worse thing on earth.

He's honestly not bad as all these reviews are making him out to seem. I actually liked him. Group projects are time consuming but if you follow his framework and listen to his preferences you will do fine. Definitely not an easy A. But a B is not too difficult to get. Make sure u dont forget to put the attendance code when you get to class.
He is a tough teacher, but if you work hard and get on his good side- you're good.

Prof K is tough. He can be very blunt and mean. On the other hand, you might get lucky, and he will respect you. It really is a gamble. Take another professor if you can. The case studies aren't that bad. It is really just him that is bad. But as a person, he does seem to care, just expresses this is an odd way.

Professor Korogodsky is tough but super fair. As long as you put in the work and pay attention you can manage a B with no issues. He is eager to teach and answer questions as long as you are eager to learn. His tests were a little bit difficult, but his projects are fun.
Whatever good ratings on here for him are fake ones written by him. Dude sucks, avoid

Very mean and intimidating. You do 2 cases that he grades harshly, 2 exams and a final project. No point in trying to talk to him he'll just say to come during office hours. He will either not be there or be very dismissive when you arrive. Does not want you to succeed. Take someone else

BTE is required so there's almost no way around him but if you can take another teacher. Gives group cases that have nothing to do with class and grades them hard. He almost wants to fail some students. The course material is boring and korogodsky doesn't help. He is usually just making everyone feel awkward when he calls people out in class.

Very bad professor. Loves the tiny bit of power that has and is very disrespectful towards students. Impossible to talk to and if you try to approach him he will essentially tell you to kick rocks. Also gives impossibly hard group presentations that he will interrupt you during to nit pick. Do not take him if you have the option.
This individual should be relived of their profession in any future academic setting.
Doesn't care if you succeed.

Worst teacher I've ever had, hands down. The dude is just plain rude to students and doesn't seem to actually care at all about teaching the class. UM should be ashamed of themselves for offering this fool employment. He belongs in a kindergarten classroom (as a student) because all he does is act like a child.

Prof Korogodsky is straight-up mean. He constantly nit-picks every part of your group projects, will ask you questions in the middle of your presentation and will make you sit down mid-presentation if he doesn't like your answer. Don't bother trying to get away with someone signing you in cause he'll catch you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor K, is a nice guy, the class material is not hard at all, tests are memorization heavy but everything can be found on the slides. He is tough with the presentations and group projects, get a good team and prepare well, tests are super easy! All multiple choice.. I would choose another Professor but if youre stuck with him its not bad

Usually, I say to take these ratings with a grain of salt, but every rating of this professor is absolutely accurate and true. I did end his class with an A, but that was definitely not expected and it was not without borderline trauma. He belittles students, and worse than that, I genuinely don't think I learned anything valuable from his class.

Comes off as rude but is funny and nice if you get to know him. Despite kind of liking him as a person, trust me, DON'T take his class. Mostly group work. BY FAR hardest class I have ever taken in my life. Was an A student w/ 4.0 gpa but got a B. It was so hard and I expected to do even worse. Devoted most of my time to his class. Avoid it.

he loves to belittle students. sometimes he has a funny side, but 99% of the times I felt miserable and terrified of him. his group projects have unrealistic expectations, he is never satisfied with anything you present or do. there was not a single person in the class who met up to his standards.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He does not care about his students at all. He will belittle you in front of your peers till you feel worthless. All he cares about is yelling at you for no reason. Sad how so many of the professors in the business tech department are horrible. Anything you say in his class will not be right as long as he teaches.

first group presentation is graded very heavily. Expects you to know every little detail when presenting ur slide. I suggest sharing ur presentation twice before ur date. Strict with attendance if everyone starts sharing the code. A lot of people dislike him because he likes to criticize people's presentations. I don't suggest taking his class

AVOID AT ALL COSTS. The worst professor I had at UM. Extremely disrespectful towards students and loves to embarrass people during their presentations in front of the class. Gives way more work than the other professors.
This professor has such unrealistic standards for his students. The group projects have nothing to do with the class they are just to help with his ego. Avoid taking him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is a very smart and well-educated person.  However, he creates unrealistic expectations for students when it comes to group projects and exams.
