Most of your grade is made up of multiple choice exams, at-home online quizzes, and problem sets. Go to TA sessions for help with the problem sets, they will guide you through them. Attendance is mandatory, so show up and pay attention or he will cold call you. Overall, if you take notes during lectures and study for the exams, you will do fine.

The grade all comes down to practice sets and the two tests. Study hard for tests, the quizzes are online, he is funny, hard to focus, but cold calls random people, especially if they look like they aren't paying attention.

take home quizzes are easy. The exams are now in person but on your computer (lockdown browser) he takes attendance through iclicker. Very boring but easy class. Make it look like you're paying attention and he will never call on you.

2 exams, multiple choice, on lockdown (in person). Quizzes r take home and the problem sets (hw) r v easy. He RARELY assigns everything so this class is lowk a breeze. BUT he LOVES calling on ppl randomly who r talking or on their phones. Sit in the back if u don't wanna get called on. Very slow course, lectures r boring and he's hard to understand
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures aren't that interesting, but chill professor. He will call you out if he thinks you're not paying attention or talking. All quizzes are online and take home and all exams are online, but in person. He lets you have a one-page cheat sheet for the exams. Super easy class and nice professor.

The class was easy to get an A but lectures were boring and hard to get through. I had to play subway surfers on the side just to pass the time. He tries to make it interesting by calling on random people or going on tangents about random things. The directions for the research paper we had were also very unclear.

Professor Nelson is great! He is a funny guy. I took two of his classes, ECO 211 and ECO 212, and they were both easy. Exams are online and he does not assign a lot of work. I definitely recommend taking him for any economics classes he teaches.

Fun prof and makes an effort to get to know you. It's hard to know what's on the exam and doing the readings does not help, so be sure to study the content he puts in his lecture notes (posted online) outside of what he writes on the slides. HW is light and incredibly easy. One group project at the end. In person final with all other exams online.

Online class super easy. Makes camera on and attendance counts. 5 problem sets (homeworks), 4 tests including final (20 questions and 20 minutes), group project at the end. First two tests r easy and third is harder. Tests are online and not proctored or recorded! would 100% recommend, must take him if u take this class! He's also nice and funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Nelson is a really great guy. He cares about his students and wants them to do well. Most of the tests are online, and he provides plenty of prep material. Take his class - he is the best option in the department.

Just not an engaging teacher at all, you wont really learn anything. Hes a good guy, but macro is somewhat of a complex topic and he doesnt teach it well. I would not recommend him, his class is an unnecessary struggle.

Quizzes are confusing and not very related to lectures. Lectures are not helpful and he just goes on rants. You have a lot of grades including  problem sets, attendance, an essay and quizzes. However quizzes are sometimes online at home but in person online is hard, only 1 cheat sheet for so many notes and not usually related questions.
Very lecture heavy and lectures can be pretty boring but exams are all online, take-home, and non-proctored. Professor goes on tangents a lot talking about other things but overall pretty chill.

Professor Nelsons class itself is very lecture based, so it isn't the most engaging. The exams used to be take-home online which was great, but he switched it to in-person which made it a lot more challenging. If there's a professor you can actually learn from rather than memorizing and self-studying, I would do that.
Professor Nelson's ECO211 class is a breeze - just show up and stay engaged. Exams are a breeze, and Unstuckstudy can help with study prep. Boring lectures, but an easy A if you pay attention.
Very skibidi

Really great professor, tends to openly cold call people in class. His lectures are comprehensive and include great definitions for the test and a better understanding of the field. Not too many assignments outside of the problem sets other than the readings.

This class was so easy, all you had to do was show up and after that, you could literally do whatever during class. Exams are online not cumulative and super straightforward. The lectures are super boring, so be prepared for that. If you have the opportunity to take Nelson, I would take it, this class is literally a free A.

It's just your average economics course. Attendance is mandatory and the lectures may put you to sleep, but you should pay attention as he will call you out if you aren't. Exams are 20 questions, 20 minutes on LockDown Browser, not cumulative. Do your homework on time or face 50% deduction to your score. The group research paper AI-generated.

Attendance is mandatory & participation is worth 17% of your grade. Lectures are boring, but if he sees someone not paying attention, he will call you out & embarrass you & he sometimes will call on the same kids every class. 5 homeworks - worth 30%. Exams are online: 20 questions-20 mins. 4 exams, 3 worth 10% & final worth 15% but not cumulative.

Dr. Nelsons class is very straightforward. His lectures can be boring or very entertaining at times. You need to attend class as attendance is directly part of your grade. Tests are worth 45% of the final grade 20 minutes 20 question online on a lockdown browser. This class should be an easier A than other Econ classes.

He answers emails really fast. He only gives 20 minutes for 20 question exams when you have to calculate and analyze graphs. Super annoying when you have basically no time. The class is easy. Kinda boring. He's super nice.
Super funny professor if you pay attention and catch his jokes. Material is pretty self explanatory and exams were online, only about 20 questions.
Class was kind of boring, but it is not that difficult.

Just show up to class and look interested and you will get a good grade. He will call you out if you're not paying attention or if you're talking, but other than that the class is a breeze. The exams are unproctored online which make them incredibly easy to do well on, however the class itself was super boring and I didn't learn much.

So so boring, but easy to get good grades. Exams are take home (20 min for 20 MCQ). The whole class he just yaps about the economy but he makes it super funny by calling students out. Final is also 20 min 20 MCQ & the research paper is all AI written. Show up to class & answer in class online mini quizzes (1 or 2 questions)

This class is an easy A, but there's no incentive to pay attention so I didn't learn much from the class (I'm an econ major so I low key needed to). He responds to emails sometimes and all exams are taken outside of class on lockdown browser. Super easy A, but you won't learn much.

Nelson is a great professor. Very easy class with only 6 homework problem sets and a research paper. Tests are all online, take-home, lockdown browser. Attendance is small part of grade but not mandatory. I just needed this pre-req but I didn't really care for the material, it's definitely not a try-hard class, it's easy to pass

Professor Nelson is a great professor who understands Macro very well. Highly recommend! His lectures are informative, the content is important, and he is one of the few non college robot professors at the school. He has a brain ... can't say that about most professors at UM. Take him, you will learn a lot and have interesting discussions.
Great professor, take quizes during class to ensure learning, which helps paying attention

Nelson was a good professor. There are a couple assignments (problem sets/research papers) but they're easy. Exams are online w/ lockdown and easy. Attendance is mandatory and he uses Iclicker for attendance and polling questions which is a part of your final grade. Also, do NOT let him catch you on your phone or talking bc he will call you out lol

Boring lectures and he can be rude. I thought that I would perform better by sitting in the front row of the large lecture hall but instead he always picks on the people in the front and makes it an annoyance to come to class. With this being said, the course is a breeze and it's easy to get an A, just don't sit in the front.

Nelson is quiet, but he makes the concepts super easy to understand. Show up to class and you will do well, the assignments and tests are easy. However, he will call you out in front of everyone if you're not paying attention to his lectures. Would take again.

The only reason Professor Nelson has a good rating is because all of the exams are online and you can basically cheat your way into an A. If that sounds perfect for you that's great, not judging, but if you want a good professor who you can actually learn from he is not for you.

Professor Nelson is hilarious, and he does an overall solid job of teaching. He isn't afraid to call out distracted/distracting students in class, but it is easy to get on his good side if you just stay silent and not be obviously distracted. Quizzes and tests are a bit difficult but still easy to do well in the class.

This class with Professor Nelson is very easy to do the work and you will get an A, if you don't understand problem sets go to TA sessions they will give the answers. Exams are taken home so not difficult, attendance is mandatory for his lectures. His lectures are boring and are not useful for learning so I recommend taking someone else.

Show up to class, and this is a free A. The exams are online, and the homework is take-home too. There are resources to help you if you happen to not get everything from his lectures, but the subject material is so easy you might not even need the textbook. Nelson is also a good teacher himself. Take his class if you want an A with little effort!
Calls on people in class but such an easy grader.

Thought i was going to do alot worse than I acutally did. tests are the hardest thing imo cause u only get 20mins to do 20n questions even tho other people say they are really easy. i hink reading th4 book helped alot cause i couldmnot pay attention his class.

A easy, but informative economics class. All his assignments are online, but you do have to show up for attendance as he uses iClicker and does in-class polls through it. 10/10 recommend though, interesting and fun lectures

i dont understand anything he says in class. but I just do the homework (5 assignments a semester) and I have a good grade. also tests and final is online so that's easy. would take again only because of the online tests and final
Augustine really the GOAT. If you an econ major and really want to learn something don't take him, but if your just taking him for Gen Ed's, easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely hate him. He's catty and grumpy, calling out students in a 100+ person class for sleeping/talking/not paying attention, insisting that all eyes are on him all the time. Attendance is mandatory, he tracks it through an app that uses location services, but the lecture is just him reading a powerpoint he'll post online anyway. He sucks.

I actually have never found a professor I dislike more. He is not engaging and goes on tangent after tangent. He will call on students randomly to answer, or call you out if you are talking / sleeping / look disengaged. Don't recommend.

Very easy class. Grades are based on 4 tests that all have a practice set and on Problem sets. These sets might be tricky, but there are TA sections that basically guarantee a 90 if you attend. Gave extra credit just for rating him at the end of the semester.
attendance is mandatory but tests are online and remote and his work is very easy

Very kind professor. 30% of the grade is problem sets, which have TA sessions that help out with them. There are four quizzes including the final, which are all online via the lockdown browser. Overall very easy class and I will definitely be talking Professor Nelson again for Macro next semester! Participation matters via IClicker.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nelson is one of my favorite professors here. His exams are online with a lockdown browser. You get a couple of homeworks and then it's 3 or 4 exams. Attendance is mandatory cause he takes polls during class to see if you are really there or not. Super easy and a great guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great teacher if economics is not your major. I did a high school eco class and it covered all of the topics we went through. The quizzes and assignments range from incredibly easy to really hard. Go to the TA sessions and do the practice tests and you will be fine

If you're looking for an easy A with minimal effort, definitely take this. I am not a business major, but still understood all the content clearly. All the tests are online and problem sets are weighted greater than exams. Also, take advantage of the TA sessions, they're really helpful to complete problem sets.
All tests are online. Got an A and learned nothing.

Nelson is such a good professor. Definitely take him if you are taking the class as an elective or requirement for a major. Funny and a good guy, super easy hw and online tests. Textbook is not really used so you can buy it if you want, but you don't have to. Take him over Spiegelman.

Nelson is a funny, nice man who is very experienced in his field. Although I received an A in the class, I cannot tell you a single thing about economics. His lectures are very slow so its hard to stay focused and he does not provide much help for the assignments, but just go to the TA office hours. Tests not super easy but are online.

Nelson is the best Econ teacher. Tests are all online. It is difficult to stay focused during his lectures so reading the textbooks along with the lectures is a good idea. Problem sets can be difficult however there are online sessions that help. Go to them and you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nelson is a good guy, but he can be a little passive-aggressive at times and call u out in front of the whole class. The class itself is pretty easy, just sit there and get through it you'll be fine.

If you want to just take this for credit and do not care about the material then take him. Do not take if you actually want to learn. He also mask shames even though it was optional for most of the semester. While it was required he would throw a fit if you had it slightly below your nose 150 ft away from him... Take if you want easy grade.

30% of the grade was problem sets, and all of them are easy and you should get an A. Tests are hit or miss because a lot of them are very easy, but they're only 20 multiple choice questions so if you get a few wrong you're kind of screwed. He's a nice enough guy if you reach out to him, he wouldn't bump up my grade but no hard feelings.

Professor moved all our tests online (via lockdown browser but no camera on) and changed our final to a group research project. He was always nice, just don't talk while he was talking. The class was very easy, but if you actually want to learn anything, take a different professor.
GOAT

Amazing professor and best at UM. Take him if you have a chance for 211 or 212. If you really want to learn though, take someone else. Powerpoint heavy, but exams are all online including the final! Chill dude, as long as you complete the problem sets and do well on the tests, you will end with an A. Love you nelson!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Man is goated. Easily the best professor on campus and an easy class as long as you show up and complete the problem sets which are worth a large percentage of your grade but you just have to complete it. Take him for ECO 212.
Best Professor on campus

if you pay attention youll pass but its hard to pay attention because its painfully boring. Theres practice exams before exams, everything is online, homework is based on completion, and he posts all the ppts online. If you struggle with econ, this isnt the best choice. If youre good with econ, you should be fine taking Nelson.

Professor Nelson is a nice person and cares about making topics accessible to everyone. However, this results in painfully slow and uninteresting lectures. Tests (including final) are online and he gives practice tests before each one. Problem sets are graded just on completion. Very easy class; wouldnt take if you want to genuinely learn.

Makes sure that every student is on same page before moving on. If you pay attention, it will be an easy class to get an A in. Online exams. Practice tests, problem sets, and revision sheets to help study. Sometimes not helpful when answering questions. Textbook not necessary but helpful if lost. Power-point heavy, can get boring but good overall.

All tests are online and you can take them where ever you want, which of course is an advantage. The class is very lecture heavy so it gets boring pretty fast. Professor Nelson himself is an ok professor, but I feel like he gives his students sass when they ask a question in class.

Prof. Nelson is a fantastic professor and makes the content taught as simple as possible without missing any details. Lectures can be slow if you are not super engaged, but any content you may miss is on his powerpoints. Would 100% take again.

I had taken econ in high school however his syllabus is helpful. Problem sets followed by tests help effective learning and fair grading. Tests are online and not in class. He wants to help students do well and teaches well. Definitely take this class.

He is so funny haha whenever someone's phone goes off he goes "some noise?" and I just think it's the funniest thing ever. Anyway exams are easy and repeats questions from the practice exam. Boring but you can get an A.
Very little homework. exams were online. pretty cool dude, but I honestly didn't learn much.

Only grades were 4 tests that cannot be passed by paying attention in class. Professor Nelson expects his students to have a level of undertsanding in macro that can not be attained until post undergrad status. He is a very nice man and makes himself avaible for help, but even after asking for help, his tests contained completely new content.

I liked him as a professor. He is funny and kind. Not much to his class, not gonna lie, I don't even know what the class was about. All he says in class is GDP and an occasional Trump joke. I couldn't understand the material but somehow did well on my exams. Class is based on 4 exams. Definitely didn't show up to his class and only went remote.

His tests new super manageable. Go to his lectures make study guides and guaranteed pass. Do not expect to pass with no effort. He is an amazing professor and completely worth it for average hard working students. Attendance isn't mandatory, no homework only problem sets once in a while.
Greatd professor, even though class isn't mandatory he makes it really fun you'd want to go.

Nelson is a great guy but doesn't inspire or have quality teaching skills. He reads off powerpoints and has a daily tangent about Trump and the American political system. Often times I feel like it's a political science class, not economics! No need to show up to class, no other students will be there

Attendance isn't mandatory, homework is easy, lectures arn't mandatory. He knows the most out of everyone I know about monetary policy. He would probably be better working for the Federal Govt in the Treasury or FDIC/similar. If you show up to class daily and take notes, automatic A. If you go to half the classes, you will struggle for a B(Like me)

to do well on his exams, do the practice problems he assigns and the end of chapter questions on mindtap. His final exam was litterly the end of chapter exam questions. Study those and just skim through his powerpoints the book isnt needed. The first exam had 3 chapters but the last one had like 7 so study a little bit each week. do this for an A

Professor Nelson doesn't take attendance and you can do pretty well on Exams if you do the homework. Your grade only comes from Homework and 2 exams. He's a good teacher and thouroughly explains all the material. You HAVE to study for exams of you wont get a good grade. He does curve the mid-term.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Really cool and funny guy. Didn't learn one thing. No one goes to class for that reason. He can't teach and just reads of powerpoints. He even started writing his own notes to force people to come to class and that didn't work either. There's a solid curve, HW and a group project (which was a diaster). I would take again b/c easy B+/A- for no work.

This guy is terrible. Rambles for the whole class period off topic. When he decides to be on topic he reads from the slide in a droning voice, but eventually leads off topic which just confuses you. Only 2 homeworks and 2 exams That are very short and easy. If you're forced to take this class better to just study on your own and skip his lectures.

If you want an semi-easy A take this class. There are two tests and two problem sets (only about 3 questions, easy grading). His lectures are very boring and he just follows the powerpoints (he posts these online & attendance isn't mandatory). If you feel confident in Macro it is really not necessary to attend class. He's alright, nothing special.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Avoid this teacher. He is a horrible teacher that reads directly off the powerpoint. He doesn't know how to explain the material. His tests are impossible and are on stuff he doesn't even teach. Nelson is a horrible teacher I do not suggest you take him.

Awesome professor.  I really enjoyed taking him, and I thought he was very good at explaining things to us. He also went out of his way to meet after class and explain anything to anyone.  I would take him for 302 100% if he is available.  Great guy to - you will learn a lot of real world stuff!

By far the worst teacher I have ever had. I am an Econ major, and I have learned absolutely nothing in this class. He is all over the place. Sends out review sheets the night before the exam, with wrong answers. Emails after class started saying that he is going to miss class. Does not explain anything. I DO NOT recommend taking him.
Minimal work, tough tests, powerpoints are all online. Lectures are long because he goes off on tangents but he is quite knowledgeable in economics and pretty funny. I really enjoyed his class.
Great Teacher, No homework, funny!
Very easy class, attendance not mandatory, notes are online.  A couple 3 problem rlly easy hw assignments.  Talks a lot about economics and finance but not rlly on the stuff he tests on.
If you do all the problem sets that is given, you will do well on the test. I barely go to class and does all his problem sets and also look at the answers he posted and did very well on his test.

He seemed to not really be focused on the material he was given to teach. He gives 2 tests and 2 problem sets. The thing is the the first and second test were vastly different formats. Vague questions are asked on both the test and in class. He's funny but not all there. And he hates when you text.
Hilarious guy, great accent. Teaches very slowly very easy to understand. Tests very predictable and doable

He's a super chill guy, who loves to talk about weed. He presents the material in a manner that is easily comprehendible. However, you will have to do most of the studying on your own. His exams aren't MC, so it's crucial for you to memorize the formulas. Honestly, if you memorize the formulas you'll do well. I'd recommend him! Simply B, the least.

The material is well presented. Provides detailed answer keys to the problem set. You have to study it. The second section of the course is more difficult. But, he is helpful in office hrs and outside of class. There is class presentation from a set of interesting topics. I learned a lot. Great and friendly professor. But, you have to study.

Professor Nelson is very helpful outside of class in helping students understand the material. The material presented in class is fairly straightforward. Although I rarely showed up to class, I found this class to be very entertaining. If you want an easy A, take this class. For your GPA's sake, you will not regret it.

Thinks he's teaching math class with advanced calculus and logarithm derivations. Makes you do tedious derivations of formulas for no reason. The rest of class you learn nothing. Difficult for no reason and boring. Also, first half of the class is insanely easy and second half is impossible. Second half consists of 80% of the total info covered.
He is helpful, nice and the best professor ever.

This guy is honestly one of the worst professors I have ever had. He assigned a major project last minute and told us at 9:30pm the night before that our project would be due the next day. Terrible teacher, unorganized, boring, bad at explaining concepts. Problem sets are different than the test, which he doesn't review for. Avoid. Avoid. Avoid.
Has the best accent I've ever heard! Could listen to him speak all day! Class is easy, kinda funny! Tests are exactly like the problem sets! Hard to do poorly!

Dude is great. Doesn't teach much but it's easy to get a good grade, his tests are literally the problem sets. Go to class because he'll like you and drop into office hours once or twice just for the hell of it. Talks about weed a lot. Chill dude, easy A. Took him for 211 and 212
HIS PROBLEM SETS ARE THE TEST. TAKE HIM!
I hated Nelson. He hates it when a student argues with him and dislikes interruptions from cell phones, etc. His tests are by the book and his actual classes were a waste of my time. Avoid taking him

If you come to class he will be nice to you, and you can tell he gets aggravated with the people who don't show up. The test are really easy, just study his power points.  He goes through the material slowly, and you never get through everything he has listed on the syllabus. And he wont test on anything he didn't present to you in class.

Took him based on earlier reviews & wish I hadn't. Puts very little effort into teaching the class. Reads directly off the power points. I waste my time attending his class when I could get the same info by staying home and reading the book/power points. Easy to get a high grade from the way he curves the grading system - 80 and above is a B
Professor Nelson is a really good teacher. He is very funny and his clases are very interesting. The final for this class is very hard, but he curves.
Prof Nelson is great!  Easy class, his problem sets ARE the test.  TAKE HIM!

Has somewhat of an accent, definitely understandable. Talks about pot a lot, like every class. Good guy and likes to joke around, get on his good side. I missed about half of the classes and still ended up with an A...he knows it a mandatory class and makes it as painless as possible. Take if open for an easy grade.

He is the best professor I've ever had. His classes is clear and easy. His PPT is clear as well. I got 93 at his exam. He will review before the test. 5handouts(HW) in a  semester, which are easy and can find out in his PPT. Study his handout and ppt, you will get great grade on ECO 211.  I really want take his eco212 next semester.
Great teacher, easy class.  Grading consists of two homework assignments (20%) a midterm (40%) and a final (40%).  Tests are not cumulative and not hard.
very boring class/hard to pay attention to

While some of his problems can be a little tricky, the tests are easy as along as you do the problem sets and pay attention in class.  He's a really nice guy and willing to help and does his best to make class entertaining.  It was my easiest A at UM, and I would recommend him.

Dude is always stoned all he talks about is pot he's a terrible teacher and shows no interest in his class. He's pretty easy though and an overall nice dude you won't hate him but you won't learn sh*t
Best professor ever... Very helpfull. Knows the material very well. Very fun class. Highly recomended.

This professor is terrible. He treats his class as if it were a joke. He will let you know what each assignment entitles the day before it is due. The final was on material that the textbook did not cover and he never went over in class. He is not available to students and he even admits he doesn't care about the class. Avoid if you can.
Teaches from powerpoints that he posts on Blackboard. The coursematter can be a bit confusing at times but he's a good teacher. Posts review sheets before exams

Although microeconomics isn't a difficult subject, he tries to make it as tricky as possible. However, he is a nice guy and willing to help. I got a B on both tests, and somehow ended up with an A in the class, which I think was due to the fact that I attended office hours so frequently.

Horrible, you dont learn. Gives tests and problem sets on what he doesnt teach. expects you to know problem-solving w/o going over logic in class or even giving answers to book problems. Don't listen to other reviewers. I'm sure you can find a better eco prof. I'm getting an A but didnt learn a thing.

great!!!!! must take if you do not anything about econ. I got a 72 on the first test then made sure to do all the practice problems and then i failed the final  but i still got a b+......gotta taKE HIM  HES GREAT
very good
aasa

Nelson is the MAN! Defintely take his 3 hour class once a week and joke around with him. If he likes your class, your tests will be easier and he will help you more on them.  Do the problem sets on time and problems in the book because similar ones appear on the tests.

take night class, get on his good side, make sure the class doesn't piss him off. he gives different tests to different classes depending on how much he likes the class. awsome guy, funny, smart, and you can learn alot. NELSON IS THE MAN!
Great professor
No Comments

Professor is slightly hard to understand, and the class is boring.  It is good to see him during office hours, but even then he does not help you too much.  There is a large grading scale curve which helps, but his tests are difficult.  Overall, I do not recommend his class.  P.S. He loves his coffee!
Good teacher, cool guy, awesome grading curve makes it impossible to fail. Easy to do very well on all the tests, too. Nice guy if ur not an annoying person, then he'll crush you
very annoying accent. makes everything so much more complicated than it really is with all his problems on the board.

Awesome guy. One of my favorite teachers. Is extremely nice as long as your not annoying. I attended all his classes and got As on the tests. Its all from the notes. No outside of the classroom work compared to other ECO302 classes. He gives out problem sets but doesnt really grade them. I would DEFINATELY recommend him.
Funny teacher, Put some effort and you can get an A.
No Comments
DR. Nelson is very nice.  You don't have to buy the book.  He might just be confusing at times, but if you let him know he'll explain again.

Really great professor for this class. You do have to attend class(not because he takes attendance) because everything is from his lecture. He does not use the book(save money). Plus he knows it is a required couse and will help you to get an A if you try.

Professor Gudridge is the worst professor I have had in my 20 years of education. He knows absolutely NOTHING about torts and it is shameful that the university lets him teach at all. The class was an absolute waste of time (which he said so himself) and leaves you to teach yourself the material for the bar exam.
Complete waste of a class. Did not teach any doctrine nor lead any meaningful discussions. No syllabus and an open-AI exam shows the quality of his class. Needs his tenure revoked.
Week 2 and still no syllabus

You cannot become a lawyer without this course. This is the most important class of all of law school, so please be prepared to become inspired and motivated!! His lectures are very important to attend because they are so organized, clear cut, and concise. I didn't realize how much there was to learn until I took this course.  Thank you so much.

Do not take this professor under nay circumstances! Attendance is not mandatory, however, the times you do go will consist of him just rambling on aimlessly about whatever he finds interesting that day. He assigns some cases to write about and doesn't give any guidance or structure. He's borderline senile! Avoid at all costs.

Do not take a class with him. Attendance is not necessary, don't read anything... will not correlate with your grade. In office hours, he just talks at you (like lectures). Avoid at all costs. Also, why is he still a professor here?

Professor Gudridge is brilliant and can chat for hours but that does nothing to help you prepare for his exam. All he cares about is your opinion. Doesn't care about holdings or black letter law, just your opinion on the Justices' opinions. Great man, awful professor. Buckle up.
He is a genuinely nice guy who really cares for his students. That said, I, and many others, have no idea what he is teaching in class.

Very smart man and very entertaining. He's not very concerned with black letter, he approaches things more as an academic (compare this to that).  Attending class doesn't matter much if you have a good outline. He gives you a heads up on the material the final exam will cover (usually material at the end of the semester). Exam was reasonable.
Very Brilliant, but never prepared for class.  All you need to do well in class is Chemerinsky's Hornbook.
You won't learn contracts.  Cool guy, bad teacher.

He rambles and is a genius, but unfortunately listening to him doesn't seem to help at all on Exam. His assignments were manageable, however the top of the curve on his exam never cracked the book. Save the money and just read Case Notes/High Courts.

had him for con law II...he is so unprepared for class and just babbles on about random stories...i went to class consistently but regretted bc after all that time i still had no useful notes or any idea about his perspective on the material...he tells you not to come to class and listen to him!
Good professor if you like 'em theoretical. His exam was nice and fair.
love, love him. brilliant but not arrogant. absent-minded professor. doesn't care if you read or ever come to class, but if u pay attention in class u don't have to read and u'll do well.
I thought the material was easy but then he gave me a big fat C.  boooo!

Very intelligent man.  Class is very interesting, especially those with a passion for history.  Still, he can be a bit tangental.  Sometimes its hard to put a structured outline together with his lectures.
Makes the subject matter interesting; easygoing; way more than fair

Makes class fun with his off the cuff remarks about the facts of each case covered.  His exam makes you think, but usually there are no surprises as he gives you huge hints as to what the questions will be.  Overall good guy and a fun professor.

a great teacher, she is super caring and compassionate but can be unorganized at times. her grading criteria is not clear either but she will discuss your grade if you ask her. only one test - the midterm which was kind of hard but she was not a harsh grader with this. just participate and talk to her outside of class. but the TA teaches you more.

One of my favorite professors ever. As long as you do the work and show that you are putting in effort, you will do fine. She is willing to help you, you just gotta show that you genuinely want to do well. Also extremely kind and understanding. Yes, she can be a bit disorganized, but overall I learned a lot in her class.

Professor Presson is absolutely amazing and cares so much about her students. She truly wants every single one of her students to succeed. Professor Presson makes sure that everyone understands the material. I feel confident that anyone who took this class will have the skill set to succeed in future broadcast classes. She is awesome!

Professor Presson is one of the nicest professors I've ever had. That being said, she caused me a lot of stress from not following her syllabus, not giving back grades for months and just being generally discombobulated. She has great knowledge and means well, but she's not organized enough to be an effective teacher.

I absolutely loved Professor Presson's course. She was always willing to help with any concerns or questions that I had. Some may say she doesn't give enough feedback, but if you show that you want to improve and take the initiative to send her an e-mail and ask, she will give you very detailed feedback. I definitely recommend her for JMM245.

Professor Presson is one of the kindest professors I have had. She made her class fun and was always helpful and happy to meet with you outside of class. She is a pretty easy grader but does not give specific feedback. If you really want to improve your production and video skills I would recommend another professor.

I love professor Presson. She really cares about her students and really tries to help you through the difficult class. She gives really good feedback on the projects and really wants to help you improve on everything.

reviews.comment: Never prepared and overall didnt learn much.
DO NOT TAKE!!!!! Everyone says she is the "easier" option, which is true but she is hard, confusing and does NOT know what is going on.

Professor Presson is incredibly sweet and cares about all of her student's success. Attendance is mandatory because of all of the hands on work in the studio. It is a fun class and she makes it easier as JMM245 is a difficult class. A lot of group projects and working with equipment outside of the classroom.

The kind of class you can't be absent, heavy material and requires in person studio participation. Be on time, participate. JMM245 is the hardest class in Comm. Lots to learn. She gave good feedback on projects and was always helpful. Don't worry much about grade, do your work and she is generous when grading. She's always available to help!

Dr. Q is a great prof. Pay attention in class, she doesn't give a study guide, but literally tells you what to focus on for her exams and got an A everytime. No breaks in class and some lectures are a bit slow paced but she tries to finish early. She's really nice if you do reach out for help!

Dr Quinones is a very motivational lecturer; I left her course engaged and empowered. The content is useful for real-world application to our disciplines. One specific project in the course was extremely fun to do so it made for a breath of fresh air in a busy courseload otherwise. She's a very kind professor and answers emails promptly.
I would take a different professor if I can. The experience I had was not great.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Quinones is a good lecturer. Unfortunately, the majority of my class wouldn't show up for the lecture because participation/attendance did not matter. She's approachable. Her exams are straightforward. I wish she had given us study guides, but other than that, it was a decent class.

I learned so much from what I thought would be a boring class. The journals at the beginning are tedious but once you do all that work is much easier from there. The CV and portfolio are very helpful later when I obtained a job. She gives great feedback. The exams are super easy and she tells you what to focus on. Take professionalism with her.

You can see how much she is passionate about Pediatrics. BEST TEACHER EVER! Exams were so straightforward and easy. She tells you exactly what you need to focus on for the exams. She is caring and very bright and loves to teach the next generation of nurse practitioners.

She genuinely cares about her students learning. Exams were so straightforward and easy. I learned so much this semester. She's very serious and lectures are a tad boring, but 10/10 I would take her again

(i took NUR317 but it wouldnt let me put that) I loved this class and this professor. It is mainly her lecturing and rarely any work other than a small quiz at the end of each class, so you have to go to class, as you cant make up quizzes ugh. but the class is so interesting and she lectures in such an engaging way!

I have never dealt with a more condescending and unaccommodating professor in my life. She can make you feel extremely small with her attitude and air of superiority. She will disregard your feelings and is rigid. Awful professor who needs to check herself and actually try to help students. The way she says things to you is cruel and unnecessary.

Felt a little messy, and almost too easy at times-- would have liked to go more into depth about content. Not much feedback was given on assignments. All you really have to do is go to class and turn in the assignments.
The BEST professor, so so sweet and caring! Her pop culture class is so much fun and I learned a lot. Please take her!!!!!
Super manageable class with only 3 individual assignments and a few group assignments. She takes attendance, but you can easily do other homework in class. Shes super sweet and helpful, take her!

AMAZING. I was so worried about this class and it turned out to be the easiest class. Actually learned stuff. She is organized like no one, and will give you your work back in seconds. I got to work on group projects in class. She was so organized we even finished earlier. You will love her. Knowledgeable!!

professor Li is super nice and the class is very easy. you will get A if you submit all the work correctly. Shes very understanding, flexible and responsive on emails. definitely take her if you need credits. theres never any daily homework except when theres group projects or papers and she gives you a week to complete tests which are open note
An easy grader and caring to students, love her!
This class was easy, fun, entertaining and honestly good all around!
Do not recommend. The class was made far more complicated and difficult than it needed to be. I was originally registered for a different section with another professor, but was moved into this one.

Course expectations and grading criteria were often unclear. More detailed rubrics and assignment guidance would have been helpful. Communication regarding questions could be difficult at times. The material itself was manageable, but the overall course organization made it challenging to understand expectations.

reviews.comment: Absolutely don't recommend at all. Avoid at al costs.

reviews.comment: Easy for stem majors who need to get 106 outta the way. As long as you show up, smile, and nod he will always give you an A-, he doesnt believe in giving students more than a 95 tho
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The class material and work is relatively easy. However, he is such a slow reader and lectures in an incredibly boring manner. Sometimes he can make weird remarks which makes the class feel awkward. Is also blunt and can be harsh at times. Would avoid taking him as the professor for this class unless absolutely necessary.

Professor Schmitt is a very nice professor. He cares a lot about writing and it shows in his grading. Participate and go to class, do your assignments, and you'll have no problem getting a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Attendance is mandatory, but he is very understanding. He genuinely cares about his students and is engaging. The assignments are not challenging and homework is minimal. Usually a short reading every week. And a couple essays where he gives you more than enough time. I would take this class again!
clearly enjoys his job but grades essays harshly. whenever i write one i wonder what the point is because I'll probably just get a B anyways
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: He is a good professor, lectures incredibly slowly, the course work is pretty light. Gives you a syllabus at the beginning of the year along with a course pack and never deviates from it. He can be a tough grader on papers, has one group project that is an easy A and can save anyones grade. Pop quizzes are easy and only require a 2/3 to get an A+.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: good teacher and clearly passionate, reading given out is enjoyable. TOUGH grader, will knock points off on an essay for things that feel nit picky. also talks very slowly so a 50 minute class will feel like the longest class you've ever taken. funny guy, smart -- but boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Hes hilarious and considerate dont get me wrong, but he yaps. For example, he didnt ask us to read after class (we read like 10%) and gave us a pop quiz on the WHOLE story (If you miss 2/3 its -0.1 from your final GPA) He also doesnt censor words except really bad ones iykyk. He knows when hes out of line and laughs a bit. Funny guy, bad classroom.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Megan and so passed the naturalisation test together in a hotel and then went to eat Cuban food. I told her the whole story it's not her fault I lied the second time around

Man I don't think I ever meet a slower reader. Not even slow but every half sentence he stops to talk about what the half sentence was about. Super nice guy tho. Funny too. Grade is based on 3 papers, all 33% of ur grade. Straight forward on the prompts.
Overall a very boring class. He just lectures the whole time and is a tough grader on the essays. Very little work other than the 2 essays and presentation.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: this professor is a decent guy, his lectures are very boring and the papers have to be very specific to what he is asking and is a tough grader. also hands out pop quizzes for upcoming readings. overall i would look for another english class to take for a major need or requirement
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The class material itself isn't difficult but how he lectures is an actual snooze fest. He often makes uncomfortable and sometimes controversial remarks when referring to literary pieces we are studying. The class environment is not very comfortable and open; literally nobody talks. Hard grader on essays and hard to reach outside of class.

He's a nice enough guy and the class is literally just going over the assignments he tells you to read, like pre-k reading time. Highest grade he is willing to give your papers is a 93, claiming "no paper is perfect," so if you're trying to maintain a super high GPA I'd say avoid him. Still, the class is alright, an easy A if you do your best.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment:
All he does is talk in class to the 5 students that actually show up and he never stops talking. Straight up just reads and explains 3 passages for an hour and a half in the most boring way possible. He only gives up to a 93 on essays that make up your whole grade because he doesn't "want you to be lazy" for the next essay.

I would not recommend.

I found Professor Schmitt a very nice, competent and considerate professor. I'm an english minor and took him twice, you just have to read the assigned text before each class in case of a pop quiz and to be able to have an active discussion. Assigns a few papers, no exams. He's also open to giving extensions if you deserve it. Overall very engaging
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Although he's not the most exhilarating prof out there, Schmitt is great at what he teaches. If you are a good writer, you will get As on his papers. If your writing is more unsophisticated / high school level, you won't. He has interesting insights and a wealth of knowledge, so if you like English and want to learn more about poetry, take him.

He only grades this class on two essays worth 50% and 40% and he said (direct quote) "the highest grade I give is a 93 I don't even know what a better paper than that would look like". The last 10% is from "participation" but it's just a reflection of your essay grades, not your actual participation. He's also boring and sometime rude and offensive

Every class was the same. We read the stories together and he spoke for 75 minutes straight analyzing each word. It was the most boring class, but it helps a lot if you're bad at analyzing because you can take notes on what he's saying exactly and use it in your essays. Essays aren't horrible . Don't except an A, but its a low stress class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Schmitt's gotta be the most boring professor I've had at UM. You really gotta be passionate about english to listen to this guy speak for over an hour. Extremely dry, expects a weird, abnormal writing style.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do NOT take this professor. I was an english major taking the class thinking it would be easy, as it was a lower level, and found that he just gives out whatever grade he feels like without giving you any explanation or feedback. Never gives out above an A-, and will not offer feedback if you try to meet with him after class. Do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Do not take class with professor Schmitt. For a 200 level English class, his grading is unreasonable. He doesn't give anyone above a 93 and makes you really work for your grade. He sits in his seat and lectures the entire time. My least favorite professor I've ever had at UM.......

Very nice professor who lectures VERY well and will explain things thoroughly if needed! He was VERY understanding with me and even allowed me to turn in a paper or two late with only a minimal point deduction! No midterm or final! Just give him what he is looking for for in his three essays from the class chapter book and you will BY FAR pass!

Awkward demeanor for an English professor. Oddly strict for a 200 level English course, not open to anything you write about (even if it is real)/ has some fiction element to it. I understand his grading criteria, but he is almost not clear enough by the time the paper/ assignment gets returned to you (surprise grades/ nothing higher than B+)

Prof. Schmitt is a good teacher. Obvious he likes what he does. Analyzes poems amazingly. I am usually a quiet student and prefer to listen than to participate but in his class i share my thoughts/opinions He should grade more on content and quality than grammar mistakes. I would encourage him ti improve his his handwriting. Its very hard to read.

Handwriting is ilegible. He have me a B for only grammar mistakes (yes, they are important in an English class). I think the main purpose of the course is to write creatively. What matters is the content. Also, he sometimes judges your work and says you are wrong... again, its creative writing!

Likes to talk about sex. Sits at his desk, never moves for every single class and talks through the whole period. There is no variation in this course. You will walk in Professor Schmitt will be sitting in the front at his desk and we will lecture from there without writing on the board or doing anything different ever. I promise.

His class is straightforward. He will walk you through the reading and go into a lot of detail with the literary analysis. Take excellent notes during the lecture. There are three 3-5 page essays. He gives 7-8 prompts for each essay and gives you a week. Use your notes and pay attention in class; you should do well on the essays;Alwayssubmit draft
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Interesting reading material- he takes you through each work so if you show up to class, it is not hard to write the essays. There are 5 three-page essays per semester. He has clear grading guidelines, so it is hard to mess up. Really helps with learning how to analyze a text
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I would not recommend Professor Schmitt. every class is the exact same: he reads to the class and goes into great detail. The papers, while not difficult topic-wise, are graded very tough. Also, while he's not strict about attendance/punctuality, it will certainly affect your grade. If you need America Literature, look elsewhere.

Professor Schmitt is undoubtedly one of the greatest professors I've ever had the honor of working with. I took his Am Lit course this past semester and learned more about detailed literary analysis than I did in any other English course, ever. He's brilliant, hilarious, and insightful, and he truly goes out of his way to help his students excel.

There are 6 poem/story submissions due throughout the semester (No: tests final midterm or homework). You have to be a good writer in order to receive an A. Class is super boring but sometimes he will say something absolutely hilarious out of nowhere. Overall, if you aren't a very good writer (like me) but you put in the effort, you will get a B/B+

You have 3 five-page papers all semester. So there is no work. He grades them pretty hard though. You don't need to read because every class he just reads the story back to you. So class is boring and he takes attendance. If you don't mind being bored for a few hours a week take his class... You can always sleep in it

Grades so subjectively. Unless you know what he wants to hear, don't bother writing the essay. There is a "wrong" and "right" answer. If you get stuck having to take him try waiting another semester. Class isn't bad and if you get the right answer to his essay questions its easy.

Didn't like him at the beginning.  Made us buy a book of poems for $45 that he could have easily given as handouts.  The front of that book says "NO REFUNDABLE IF OPENED."  Don't like that he uses a lot of sexual metaphors because it is rather awkward.  It's a pretty easy class, but it is extremely boring.
No complaints. Great teacher, really knows his stuff and makes the class interesting. Not a hard grader and you become a better writer as the course goes on. Take this class!!

reading isnt too horrible, reads/reviews most of it in class. Take Notes on his lectures. its like a game, he hints the essay answers if you listen to the lectures. if you answer the essay question different to what he expected ur grade is affected.

Went into the class with the expectation that it wouldn't be a challenge.  It wasn't, except that his grading is unfair.  If you are a football player, you're leaving with an A.  If not, there's no way to know where you stand in the class.  Also, everything comes down to a sex metaphor in his interpretation of literature and it gets old really fast

Do not take this professor.  I worked extremely hard, am English minor, went to every class, and did all the readings prior and still only got a B.  Completely trashes your work and looks for a specfic answer in every paper.  The worest professor I took by far.  There are way easier professors in the English department.

$45 for a workbook containing****ty poems that allow no room for investigation. I echo the sentiments of a prior ranker - he favors the stupid. Don't take him if you have a mind of your own. Once you get on his bad side, there's no exit and you WILL be unhappy with your grade, though there is little on which to base it, ultimately.

10% of your grade is based off attendance and participation. Your notes wont be very useful for the topics he assigns. He wont answer questions he deems to closely related to the topic. I was surprised by the ratings on here. I went to the writing center, his office hours, and ALL the classes and didnt get an A. Im pretty sure he favors athletes.

Awesome guy who makes the class interesting. I would recommend highlighting all the things he says about the stories because he pulls this stuff for his essays that he wants written. Write well and participate and its an easy A. Highly recommend. Actually makes American Lit. interesting.

He is complete inspired by English Literature, he loves what he does. Super down to earth, extremely open to any topic you wish to discuss. He ha s a fair amount of knowledge and a such will grade your papers on that basis. NOT a super easy A, but definitely sparks interest in the course.
TAKE HIM! EASY A! just go to class, take good notes, and DONT disagree with anything he says! He practically tells you what to write for each paper.. NO FINAL EXAM! Fair grader!

He is not a horrible teacher.  His lectures are very clear and he goes over the text line for line.          Most, if not all of the class, is spent analyzing the stories read for homework.  He might go too deeply into the text, but that is a matter of opinion.  Your essays will determine your grade in his class.
No Comments
No Comments

Kiss his ass the entire semester and you will be fine, if you disagree with him too much he will give you a bad grade because he doesn't like you, he takes everything too seriously and he tries to be cool by making references to the fact that he's done drugs before.  If you want a man who probably does nothing at home but play with his 15 cats and think about how he can use his professorial power over his students all day to give himself personal gratification, than take this teacher.
No Comments
No Comments
He's easy, but if you want to learn, he's NOT the teacher to take. They should rename his class "American Literature for Dummies."
Class is definitely boring.  But he reads everything to you, so that's cool.  He likes giving A-s.  He's a good guy in general.

The class is easy, no exams, only 3 papers all semester.  However, you will find yourself struggling to stay awake during the lectures.  He makes no attempt to make the material interesting to his students.
What a joke of an instructor. Would not recommend to any student at UM if you wish to be treated with an inch of respect and courtesy.
my favorite professor

theres a lot of reading you have to do and you do have to come to class everyday to do the in class work because thats mostly what you get graded on. theres 2 major projects and thats it. hes a super understanding guy, so i say enroll in his class.

reviews.comment: Dr. Quintela was very knowledgeable and ready to help if you ever experienced any issues. He walks you through demos using the GIS software each week and his exams (1/2 based on lectures and 1/2 on practical knowledge) are very easy. There are assignments each week, but they are usually easy and you can finish some of it in class during the demos.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Quintela is a decent choice and I would take another class with him. He can be impatient at times and doesn't make much of an effort to get to know his students, but he teaches the material well. Overall I found the class really interesting and it motivated me to declare a minor in Geospatial Technology.

I loved Jorge and declared a geospatial technology minor because of this class. He is VERY knowledgeable, wants to help students learn, and sets very fair and realistic class expectations. Weekly assignments plus two exams and a final project. If you want GIS experience, this is a fantastic class to take.

IDK why he is not listed here as a professor, either way he is a good professor. Lectures are kinda drab but that is because he is extremely knowledgeable about the material he teaches. Very understanding, especially given the COVID-19 pandemic, accessible outside of class and willing to give extensions on some assignments. Overall 10/10.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: go to class and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Reaves is an amazing Fundamentals professor. Her content is engaging and her exams were very fair. If you put in time to read the textbook, practice EAQs, and pay attention in class, you will do very well in her class!
You learn alot because the class is heavy. Very organized. Understood that the semester was rough and we were trying.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Firm but fair. She's detailed oriented and is a fan of textbook reading which helped me on exams. Because that class is NOTHING but application. She really cares about her students despite what these other reviews on here might say. Just experience her class for yourself and follow the syllabus. Listen to her advice and you'll be fine.

Take at your own discretion! This course felt largely self-taught. Questions were often met with “read the textbook” rather than meaningful clarification. I found the professor dismissive, passive-aggressive, and difficult to approach. I watched several hardworking students struggle, withdraw, or fail despite genuine effort. Would NEVER take again!

Take her at your own discretion . I definitely don't recommend! She's condescending and insensitive to students.This program is designed to set you up for FAILURE. Reaves doesn't know how to teach and needs to reconsider her path. You will be teaching yourself and even that isn't enough. Also if you're not a sucker up to her you won't get by.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr.Reaves is an amazing professor and passionate about nursing. She is hilarious and lectures are engaging. Do the EAQ's and pay attention in class. Although the class might sound “easy” you should put in the effort - it will pay off.

She is a very knowledgable person. Her lectures are very in depth. Her exams are difficult BUT she does prepare you well for the HESI. She can be very dismissive and insensitive. Honestly, she is just very moody and it comes across as unprofessional. If you ask for help, or help with questions she will just tell you to read the textbook.

Test questions aren't terrible. Content sometimes alines with other classes. Lecture is only once a week. 8% weight in assignments. Cons: No extra credit or rounding. Hard to reach outside of class. Will call you out from time to time. Lots of assignments on top of clinical paperwork. 4 hours of lecture +8 hour clinical. Does NOT record lectures.
Not a fan. Very dismissive and insensitive woman. Does not seem to have much empathy or understanding towards her students. Class wasn't hard, just didn't like dealing with her at 8am every Monday.

I had Dr. Reaves for Adult Health 1 & Public Health. Nice lady, but hard to get a hold of. She leaves town a lot too. She takes her lectures very seriously so don't talk in class or she will yell at you. Do the back of the chapter questions because you will see them again. Outside of class she's really cool to talk to & gives great advice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Quesada is an amazing, caring teacher who truly supports her students. She creates a welcoming environment and always goes the extra mile to help everyone succeed. Her kindness, patience, and passion for teaching make her class a great experience. She also makes learning genuinely fun and engaging.
she makes this class waaaaaaayyy harder than it needs to be I worked so hard like countless hours of work for a bad grade.

This is the third course I've taken with Prof. Quesada-Gomez, and I have nothing but good things to say about her. I love her class, I've learned more about poetry here than in any other English class I've ever taken. You definitely have to work hard for your grade, but you truly learn a lot.

One of the most knowledgeable professors I've ever had. She can recite countless poems, some of them incredibly difficult. She is also very kind and understanding. I'm really glad I'm taking this class—she's truly the GOAT. Without a doubt, the best teacher I've ever had.

This has been the most engaging and interactive class I've taken at UM so far. The professor keeps us involved with activities that make the material easier to understand and more interesting. She clearly cares about the subject and about making sure we get the most out of the class. Her teaching style makes a big difference!
Professor Quesada is caring, knowledgeable, and genuinely funny. She makes grammar easy to understand and create a positive, engaging learning environment. I highly recommend her classes!

hard to get to know at first but in the end I saw that Profesora Quesada-Gomez cares so much about her students and always loves to see their successes. Class can be intimidating with participation and workload but she's flexible, kind, supports you if you're struggling, idk what more to say! I thought it was heartwarming to see how she cares :)

One of the most organized instructors I've ever had. While she maintains a strict classroom environment, she's incredibly supportive and sets clear expectations from day one. If you're looking to learn and progress rapidly, I highly recommend her.

This was the best Spanish course I've taken in my life. I learned more with Prof. Quesada-Gomez in one year than any other class I've taken. She was so engaging and helpful while still pushing us farther to help better our Spanish. She gave me the confidence to change from a Spanish minor to a major.

203 is rly demanding and has an overwhelming amount of work, but Quesada-Gomez tried her best to make it easier on us. She gives extra time/extensions, is understanding, and just wants you to try your best and participate. Only negative thing is she speaks loud and rly fast which made the class feel harder/more intense.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: SPA 203 is a lot of work, but Professor Quesada-Gomez is such an understanding, helpful, and organized teacher. She prepares you well for tests and exams, and you always know what to expect.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Dr. Quesada's class. It is more active than the other Spanish classes I have taken and I think that this teaching style is the best if students want to really learn a language.

Profesora Quesada Gomez was a good teacher, but made a class that should not be that hard very time consuming. Things like corrections or grammar quizzes had to be exact and there was no room for any error. You had to be 100% focused and on game 100% of the time, even just answering questions in class.

The course was extremely time consuming, and I know students felt overwhelmed by the course load; however, at the end of the day it definitely helped students develop their writing and speaking skills. Prof. Quesada-Gomez is very kind and you can tell she really cares about her students and wants every individual to succeed.
She is not very nice. SPA 201 is writing heavy, even if you know how to write in spanish but are not the best at it I do not recommend her at all.

the perfect prof. clear explanations of the concepts, good at clarifying points of confusion, emphasizes participation. she speaks in classroom-friendly spanish that is neither excessively challenging nor condescending. of course, whether your classmates stay in spanish is determined on a case-by-case basis :^) if you can take her, take her!

Overall, I really liked this course and I think I have become a much better writer in Spanish because of it. It is definitely challenging, but if you are willing to put in the work then it is worth it. I think the instructor really cares about her students.

SPA 202 is a very intensive class, and it requires reading or watching a movie before every class, including grammar assignments. If you don't do the assignments, you will not do well. However, Professor Gomez is very caring of her students, and a very very easy grader. She understands the class is difficult and she wants students to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Respected

reviews.comment: Dr. Quesada-Gomez is a great professor! I can say this is probably the hardest Spanish course I've taken at UM, however the most rewarding! She really cares about her students and wants them to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The course and its themes were well-organized. The variety of projects and discussions is something quite unique to this class. We had debates, VIP sessions to talk to students from Mexican universities, community service, position papers, in-class papers, reflection papers, and in-class presentations. Professor Quesada is amazing!

Overall, the professor was kind and helpful. The course was incredibly organized, and the content was extremely interesting and relevant. I would highly recommend this course and professor to people I know.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Profesora Quesada is okay. Her grading is fair, and there is less homework than most other Spanish classes. The 15-20 service hours required for this class is the toughest part because we had to find our own community partners. Quesada sometimes expects too much and assumes we understand things as she does, but overall she is kind.

Through her class I have found out the way in which I learn better and my passion for Spanish has grown significantly. She also brought the real world into the topics that we discussed during class, highlighted important issues, and created an inclusive environment. A lot of work, but I am so glad I decided to go into her class.

This class is very labor intensive, but she says it on the first day of class that this class has a ton of work and if you dont want that then to drop the class. Theres is a lot of homework and a lot of writing. As long as you show youre trying youll get good grades. She speaks fast but you get used to it after a few classes. Shes a nice lady.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: A scary woman at first when she decides who will stay and who will be kicked from her class, but she warms up and is an excellent professor. Accommodates you when needed. Essay heavy with exams. Lots of writing but this is a writing credit. PARTICIPATION IS REQUIRED whether you like it or not. I learned a lot from her.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Such a good professor, she cares about students so much and really wants you to improve. Lots of essays and assignments so it's a ton of work but worth it if you want to get better. reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Quesada is a very considerate and thoughtful Spanish teacher. She effectively organizes the semester into a well defined syllabus and schedule at the beginning of the year. Even with the unexpected changes to the class environment, she was still able to complete the original class curriculum, with just as much rigor and interest.

If you are genuinely passionate about Spanish and ready to improve your skills, Prof. Quesada's class is the place for you! It can be a lot of work, but it really is doable no matter your major. She is intimidating at first, but if participate and are on top of your work, she is very helpful and kind as well as an engaging teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I have had Quesada for the past two semesters for Spanish class. She is sweet and is willing to work with her students so that each person gets just as much out of her class. She will always be there to help you, and makes getting an A in Spanish easy as long as you show that you are trying.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: When I began my Spanish career with Sra. Quesada she encouraged me to switch to a different class because my spanish was "no bueno." I stayed in her class and I'm glad I did. reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Gomez really cares about her students and does want you to do well. reviews.comment: She really wants everyone to learn and is passionate about teaching. My Spanish speaking and writing has improved greatly because of her.

reviews.comment: She's awesome! I'm taking her again next semester.

reviews.comment: I like this teacher and think she care about every of her students and I can see her goal is really let us make progress. I learned a lot from this course with the help of her. Highly recommended teacher!

Professor Gomez is absolutely amazing. She is so clear when she explains information in class. She takes the time to make sure everyone understands the grammar and vocabulary concepts. She does reviews before each exam and she prepares students really well to excel. I would definitely recommend her!

I had Prof. Quesada last semester and I loved her! She made me want to learn french even at 9 am. I liked that there were many little assignments, because it made me practice my french throughout the semester. I never expected to improve so much.

Hardest professor I have taken at UM but, for me at least, that is a challenge. Doctora Quesada Gomez has been more than helpful. She is always there to challenge students but pick them up when they are down. reviews.comment: She is not only a very good professor, but she cares about helping her students to succeed and be interested in the course. Señora Quesada is extremely helpful and understanding, really friendly and warm. She is a very caring professor who wants to see yo do well in her class. I really appreciated her methodology to teach us. Her extra material helped me to improve my vocabulary and study for the exams.

I thoroughly enjoyed this class. There was a lot of material and sometimes the workload got a bit more than what I expected but it was good and necessary to fully learn the material. Prof. Quesada expected a lot of us, but in the end it was for our benefit. Her humor and friendly attitude made the class really enjoyable.

I love Profesora Catalina Quesada Gomez. I took her class last semester and specifically made sure to take her course again this semester. One of the best professors I've had in my life and most definitely the best Spanish professor I have ever had. She was so nice and always willing to help. She was always so energetic. She is a very helpful teacher and is always willing to answer your questions about the class. She is also very easy to meet with during office hours and responds to emails very quickly. I think she cares about her students. I really enjoyed having her as a teacher.
She was very knowledgable and made sure to keep the class interesting and always liked to hear our feedback on what we wanted to work on. One of the, if not the best Spanish teachers I've ever had.

I loved this class! The homework load at first was a lot but it all helped me in the long run. Professor Quesada made this class very interesting and I feel that I have a much better understanding when it comes to listening and speaking Spanish. I also enjoyed learning about the cultural aspects! I would definitely recommend her to anyone.

Prof. Quesada is an amazing professor: she definitely knows her stuff. She really loves to teach and interact with students. Her class involves a lot of reading and work outside of class, but everything is really interesting. Definitely taking her next semester!

Overall pretty easy class.  There is quite a lot of busy work, but honestly you can knock it out of the way pretty fast.  I took this class along with bio, chem, and calculus and this class was a piece of cake compared to those. Her class is not easy: a lot of homework + she speaks Spanish all the time. But she makes class very interesting and fun, and she is very helpful. I learned so much with her!

She is funny; her class is interesting, and not difficult at all if you put in a little effort. She is really supportive, helpful with anything, and extremely generous with her grading. She loves to teach and she is so passionate. I love her! She is a great professor.

Professor Martinez is so sweet but sometimes makes mistakes when doing problems on the board and students often correct her. Grading is unclear and she doesn't give you your test back. This course is pretty light and easy if you have some previous Algebra knowledge.

Makes the class harder than what it needs to be. She is unaware of what she is teaching as the class is always correcting her mistakes. Overall, the class is easy but if I have not learned this information previously then it would have been more difficult.

THE BEST THE BEST!!! I love her so much! She loves teaching and we can tell that!! She explains EVERYTHING! Attend class because honestly you take so much out of it. A lot lot of homework, though. RECOMMEND!!!

Professor Sharma would explain and demonstrate ANY confusion. I had anxiety starting my sciences and he made it seem so easy this term was genuinely a breeze. I hope it stay that way lol
He was very easy going and knowledgeable! Gave clear instructions and definitely willing to answer any questions throughout class!
One of the best professors I've had. The class was organized, expectations were clear, and assignments matched what we learned.He was patient, respectful, and made the class enjoyable.

Dr. Sharma is very sweet. I took him for a CHM 113 lab previously in 2019. This semester (2021) I took CHM 221 and HHMI Lab (CHM 205). I love his caring nature. Very knowledgeable and caring, will give great feedback with total honesty. The class is very heavily dependent on your 5 independent presentations from which the average is usually a 90. Negotiation was one my favorite classes in college. It was very engaging as we simulated real negotiations every class.
